text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a washing machine that I purchased from your website and to request an appropriate resolution.

I placed the order, number 48215-US, on March 3 for a Bosch front-loading washing machine, model WAX32, at a price of $649. The purchase was paid for in full by credit card, and your confirmation e-mail promised delivery within five working days.

Unfortunately, the machine did not arrive until March 24, which was two weeks later than promised. Nobody informed me of the delay, despite two telephone calls from me, and I had to take a day off work to wait for the courier. Worse still, when the plumber installed the machine, we discovered a large dent in the left side panel and a crack in the door glass. The drum also makes a loud grinding noise whenever it is turned by hand.

I would therefore like you to collect the damaged machine and send a replacement in perfect condition within seven days. If that is not possible, I expect a full refund. I would also appreciate some compensation for the inconvenience caused.

I look forward to your prompt reply.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Harper

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to inquire about your evening course in web design, which I saw mentioned on your website. I am particularly interested in this program because I work full-time in a small retail business and would like to develop the skills needed to help improve our company website and, in time, move into a more creative role.

Although I have not studied web design formally, I already have some relevant experience. Over the past year, I have taught myself basic HTML and CSS through online tutorials, and I have created a simple website for a family friend’s café. In addition, I use Photoshop at an intermediate level to edit images for social media.

However, the website does not provide several important details. Could you please let me know the exact start date, the weekly schedule, and the total course fee? I would also be grateful for information about the course content, the software students are expected to use, and whether any previous qualifications are required.

Finally, I would appreciate knowing how to apply and whether places are still available for the next intake.

Yours faithfully,
David Miller

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the construction work that has been taking place near my home over the past month, and to ask for your assistance in resolving the problem.

A large apartment complex is being built on the vacant lot beside Maple Road. Workers frequently arrive at around 5:30 a.m., when heavy machinery and concrete mixers are switched on, and they often continue until well after 9:00 p.m. On several Saturdays and Sundays, drilling has also been audible throughout the afternoon.

The disruption has seriously affected daily life in our neighborhood. I cannot sleep properly, and I have found it difficult to concentrate during my working day. Several neighbors with young children report that their toddlers are woken repeatedly, while an elderly resident nearby has become extremely anxious and exhausted. In addition, dust and debris regularly cover our cars and windowsills.

I would therefore urge the council to contact the developer and require compliance with reasonable working hours, ideally between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. on weekdays. I would also appreciate it if an officer could inspect the site and monitor noise levels.

I look forward to your prompt response.

Yours faithfully,

Daniel Hughes

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the part-time position of weekend guide at your museum, which I saw advertised on the town library notice board last Friday. I am particularly interested in this role because I have always enjoyed local history, and I would welcome the opportunity to help visitors understand and appreciate the museum’s collections.

I believe I would be well suited to this position. For the past year, I have volunteered at the Heritage Center in my neighborhood, where I welcomed visitors, answered questions, and led short tours for school groups. This experience taught me how to explain information clearly to people of different ages and backgrounds. In addition, I am patient and well organized, and I feel confident speaking in public. I also have strong customer service skills from my previous work in a bookstore.

As for my availability, I am free every Saturday and Sunday throughout the year. I can work mornings, afternoons, or full-day shifts, and I would also be available on public holidays if required.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Morris

issues.quote: I am confident speaking in public, patient, and well organized.
issues.correction: I am confident when speaking in public, and I am patient and well organized.
issues.reason: The list mixes a participial phrase with adjectives, so the parallel structure is faulty.

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to report a bag that I mislaid on one of your trains last week, and to ask for your help in recovering it.

On Thursday, March 14, I took the 9:15 a.m. express from Boston to New York. I sat in carriage C, close to the window, and the train arrived at Penn Station at about 1:30 p.m. In my hurry to catch a connecting subway, I stepped off without noticing that I had left my bag on the overhead luggage rack.

The bag is a medium-sized navy blue leather satchel with a brass buckle and a small tear on the left strap. Inside were a silver laptop in a gray protective sleeve, a black leather wallet containing my driver's license and two credit cards, a pair of prescription glasses in a red case, and a paperback novel. The laptop holds important work documents, so its return is especially urgent.

You can reach me by telephone at 555-0143 or by email at j.harrison@examplemail.com. If the bag has been found, I would be grateful if you could send it to my home address by courier, and I will gladly cover any postage costs. Alternatively, I could collect it in person.

Thank you very much for your assistance.

Yours faithfully,
Jonathan Harrison

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to express my concern about the condition of Riverside Park, which I use regularly and which appears to have deteriorated in recent months. I visit the park four or five times a week, usually for an early morning jog, and I often return on weekends to read on a bench or meet neighbors.

Unfortunately, the park is no longer being maintained to an acceptable standard. Several trash bins overflow for days, and litter has accumulated around the playground and along the walking paths. In addition, the grass is often overgrown, some benches are damaged, and two of the lamps near the north entrance have not worked for weeks, making the area feel unsafe after dark.

I would be grateful if the department could increase cleaning and garbage collection, especially near the playground. Regular mowing, repairs to the seating and lighting, and clearer signs reminding visitors to dispose of waste properly would also make a significant difference. If possible, more frequent inspections might help prevent small problems from becoming serious.

Yours faithfully,
Michael Turner

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to report an error in the billing for my recent stay at your hotel. I hope you will be able to resolve the matter promptly.

I stayed at the hotel for three nights, from March 14 to March 17, in a double room on the fourth floor, booked under the name Daniel Roberts. The reservation number was 58213. I was very pleased with the comfortable room and the helpful staff, and I settled the bill at the front desk when I checked out, paying by credit card.

However, when I reviewed my bank statement after returning home, I noticed that the hotel had charged my card twice for the full amount of $426. Both transactions appeared on March 17, and I have attached a copy of the statement, together with my receipt, so that you can verify the duplication.

I would therefore be grateful if you would investigate this matter and refund the extra $426 to my card as soon as possible. Please also send me written confirmation once the refund has been processed. I look forward to hearing from you within the next week.

Yours faithfully,

Daniel Roberts

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing in response to the proposal to close the Westbrook Public Library. For me, this library is far more than a building with shelves of books. I use it every week to borrow materials, work in a quiet space, and access online journals that I cannot afford at home. It has also helped me improve my job skills through its free computer classes.

The closure would harm many other residents as well. Schoolchildren rely on the library for homework support and a safe place to study after classes. Older people often visit for large-print books, newspapers, and social activities, while job seekers depend on its internet access, printers, and staff guidance when preparing applications. Families with limited incomes would be especially disadvantaged.

If the town must reduce spending, there are better options. For example, it could shorten opening hours on the quietest weekday evenings, combine some administrative services with another municipal department, or delay nonessential beautification projects in public spaces. These measures would save money without removing such an important community resource.

I hope the council will reconsider this short-sighted plan.

Yours faithfully,
David Turner

Dear Ms. Harper,

I am writing to ask whether I could take a week of leave next month. My younger sister is getting married in Portland, and as I am one of her witnesses, I need to be there for the preparations as well as the ceremony itself. The family has been planning the event for almost a year, so it would mean a great deal to me to attend.

I would like to be away from Monday, March 10, to Friday, March 14, and return to the office on Monday, March 17. I have checked the team calendar, and this period does not clash with any major deadlines or the quarterly audit.

To keep everything running smoothly, I have a few suggestions. I could finish the monthly sales report before I leave and prepare a clear handover document covering my ongoing projects. Daniel has kindly offered to handle my urgent client inquiries, and I would be glad to brief him beforehand. Less pressing tasks could wait until I return, and I will also set up an automatic reply with his contact details.

Thank you very much for considering my request. Please let me know if you would like to discuss it.

Yours sincerely,
Emily Carter

Dear Mr. Harris,

I am writing about the heating in the flat, which stopped working two days ago. I tried to reach you by phone several times yesterday evening and again this morning, but I was unable to get through. The boiler appears to switch on normally, yet none of the radiators heat up, and there is no hot water in the kitchen or bathroom either.

This has become quite difficult, as the weather has turned much colder this week. The flat is especially chilly at night, and I have been waking up because of the cold. In addition, not having hot water is making it hard to shower before work and to wash dishes properly.

I would be grateful if you could arrange for someone to come as soon as possible. I will be at home after 5:30 p.m. on weekdays, and I am available at any time this Saturday. If necessary, I can also ask my neighbor to let the repair person in during the day.

Kind regards,
Emma Collins

Dear Mr. Harris,

I hope you are well. I am writing about something that has been troubling me recently, and I hope we can resolve it in a friendly way. I live in the apartment next to yours, and I have noticed that your dog barks almost continuously from the morning until the late afternoon, while you are at work.

I should explain why this is so difficult for me. I work from home as a translator, and my job requires a great deal of concentration. The barking is loud and unpredictable, so I often lose my train of thought and have to postpone important calls with clients. It has also become hard to rest at lunchtime, and I have started to feel quite tired and stressed by the end of the week.

I am sure your dog is not misbehaving on purpose and is probably lonely or bored when he is by himself. Perhaps you could ask a dog walker to visit him around midday, or leave him some interesting toys. Some owners also find that leaving soft music on helps to calm their pets.

I would be very happy to discuss this with you whenever it is convenient. Thank you for your understanding.

Yours sincerely,
Daniel Brooks

Dear Ms. Carter,

I am writing to apologize for missing the last two evening classes. On Monday I developed a high fever and a severe sore throat, and my doctor diagnosed a chest infection and advised me to stay home for several days. Although I had hoped to recover quickly, I was still too unwell to attend Thursday’s lesson.

I am concerned about falling behind, especially as the course is becoming more demanding. Could you please let me know which topics and assignments were covered in those two sessions? If there are any handouts, reading tasks, or exercises I should complete before I return, I would be very grateful if you could tell me. I can also collect any materials from the office, or I would be happy to receive them by email if that is easier.

Fortunately, I am feeling much better now, and I expect to be back in class next Monday, provided there are no further problems. I will make every effort to catch up before then.

Kind regards,
Emily Brown

issues.quote: because it was a chest infection
issues.correction: because I had a chest infection
issues.reason: The clause is illogical and awkward: a fever and sore throat are symptoms, and the cause should be stated with a personal subject; 'it' has no clear referent.

issues.quote: I can also collect any materials from the office, or I would be happy to receive them by email if that is easier.
issues.correction: I can collect any materials from the office, or I would be happy to receive them by email if that is easier.
issues.reason: The sentence mixes 'can also' with an unrelated alternative, and 'also' is illogical because no earlier collection option was given.

text:
Dear Ms. Harper,

I hope you are well. I am writing to ask whether you would be willing to provide a reference for me. You may remember me as Daniel Brooks, who worked as a sales assistant in your department at Linwood Stores from March 2019 until June 2022.

I have recently applied for the position of customer service supervisor at Greenfield Home Supplies, a regional retailer. The role involves leading a team of eight advisers, handling complaints that cannot be resolved at the counter, and preparing monthly reports on customer satisfaction. It would be a considerable step up from my current post, but I feel ready for the challenge.

I am asking you in particular because you supervised my work more closely than anyone else, and you know how I dealt with difficult situations. You may recall that I organized the training sessions for new staff and helped to reduce errors in processing returns during the busy holiday season. I believe the employer would value your opinion of those achievements.

The company would need to receive the reference by the end of the month. I would be happy to send you my résumé and the job description if that would help.

Thank you very much for considering my request.

Yours sincerely,
Daniel Brooks

text:
Dear Ms. Harris,

I am writing about the recent change to our training schedule. I have been a member of the Riverside Sports Club for just over four years, and during that time I have always appreciated how well the sessions have been organized.

However, the new training time of 8:30 p.m. on weekdays is causing difficulties for many members. Several of us work full-time and have to travel some distance to get home, so arriving at the club that late is not easy. In addition, the session now finishes close to 10 p.m., which is too late for younger members and for anyone who has work the following morning. Attendance has already dropped noticeably in the past two weeks.

May I suggest a more flexible arrangement? It would be much better to hold the main session at 6:30 or 7:00 p.m., as before, or alternatively to offer two sessions each week, one in the early evening and one later, so members can choose the most convenient option.

I hope you will consider this suggestion.

Kind regards,
Daniel

issues.quote: one early evening and one later, so members can choose
issues.correction: one in the early evening and one later, so that members can choose
issues.reason: The article and preposition are missing, and 'so that' is the more natural purpose connector here.

text:
Dear Ms. Carter,

I am writing to suggest a change that I believe could make our office a more pleasant and productive place to work.

At present, everyone is expected to be at their desk from nine to five, even when their tasks could be done just as well at other times. Many of us spend over an hour commuting in heavy traffic, and by the time we arrive, we are often tired and stressed. Several colleagues have also mentioned that the open-plan layout makes it hard to concentrate in the mornings.

My idea is to introduce flexible working hours with a core period between ten and three, when everyone would be available for meetings. Outside those hours, staff could start earlier or finish later, and they could work from home one day a week. We could try the arrangement for three months and then review the results together.

I am confident that employees would feel more motivated and less exhausted, which would improve their concentration and reduce sick leave. The company would benefit from higher productivity, and it would also find it easier to attract and keep talented people.

I would be happy to discuss the details whenever it suits you.

Yours sincerely,

Daniel Brooks

Dear Mr. Collins,

I am writing to thank you for the very pleasant stay I had at Willow Creek Guest House last weekend. I stayed for two nights in Room 4, and I really appreciated your kindness, the excellent breakfast, and the quiet atmosphere. After a long week at work, it was exactly the relaxing break I needed.

Unfortunately, when I arrived home on Sunday evening, I realized that I had left behind my navy blue leather jacket. It is a light spring jacket with a silver zipper, and there is a pair of black gloves in one of the pockets. I think I left it hanging on the wooden coat hook behind the door, although it may also have been placed over the chair beside the window.

If you happen to find it, could you please send it to my home address? I would be very grateful, as the jacket was a gift from my brother and means a great deal to me. I would, of course, be happy to cover the postage and packing costs immediately by bank transfer or any other method you prefer.

Kind regards,
Daniel Harris

issues.quote: It is a light spring jacket with a silver zipper and a pair of black gloves in one pocket.
issues.correction: It is a light spring jacket with a silver zipper, and there is a pair of black gloves in one pocket.
issues.reason: As written, the jacket appears to have both a zipper and a pair of gloves as parts of it; the gloves need a separate clause.

issues.quote: If you happen to find it,
issues.reason: The writer is certain the jacket was left behind, so "happen to find" is unsuitable and sounds as if its presence is doubtful.

text:
Dear Emma,

How are you? I'm sorry I haven't written sooner, but the last few weeks have been a whirlwind of boxes and paint. I've finally settled into my new place, so I wanted to tell you all about it.

The apartment is on the second floor of an old brick building, and it's much brighter than my last one. The living room has huge windows that look out over a small park, and there's even a tiny balcony where I've put some herbs and a chair. The neighborhood is lovely, too. There's a bakery on the corner that makes the best cinnamon rolls I've ever tasted, and a river path is only a ten-minute walk away.

Now, here's the important part: I'd love you to come and stay for a weekend! I have a comfortable sofa bed, and you'd be welcome any time next month. Just tell me which dates suit you, and I'll make sure I'm free.

While you're here, we could stroll along the river and have a picnic if the weather's nice. There's also a weekend market full of local crafts, and I've been dying to try the Thai restaurant nearby. We could even catch a film at the old cinema downtown.

Write back soon and let me know!

Lots of love,
Sophie

Dear Emma,

I am so sorry I missed your birthday party on Saturday. I had every intention of coming, but my manager called that morning to say one of my coworkers was sick, and I had to cover the evening shift at very short notice. By the time I finished, it was far too late to make it over, and I felt terrible about letting you down.

I have been wondering how everything went. Did lots of people come in the end? You mentioned you were planning a barbecue in the yard, so I hope the weather stayed nice. Most of all, I want to know whether you liked the gift from your sister, because you were so curious about what she had bought you.

To make it up to you, why don't we meet next Friday evening and celebrate properly together? I could take you out for dinner at that little Italian place you love, and afterward we could grab dessert and have a long catch-up.

I hope you had a fantastic day despite my absence.

Best,
Mia

issues.quote: why do we meet next Friday evening
issues.correction: why don't we meet next Friday evening
issues.reason: The suggestion structure is "why don't we ..."; "why do we meet" is ungrammatical as a suggestion.

text:
Dear Emma,

Thank you so much for looking after my apartment and Biscuit while I was away. I can't tell you how relieved I felt knowing he was in such good hands. He seems happier than ever, and I'm sure the extra walks and treats you gave him had something to do with it! Thanks, too, for watering the plants. They're all still alive, which is a small miracle.

The trip was wonderful. We spent ten days in Portugal, starting in Lisbon, where we wandered through the old streets and rode the famous yellow trams. Then we drove south to the Algarve and stayed in a tiny fishing village. The beaches were almost empty, the seafood was fresh from the boats, and I even managed to try surfing, though I spent more time in the water than on the board. I took hundreds of photos, so you'll have to come over and see them.

To say thank you properly, let me cook dinner for you this weekend. I'll make that lasagna you like so much. And if you ever go away yourself, I'd be delighted to look after your cat and your garden.

Thanks again for everything!

Love,
Sophie

Dear Emma,

I was so excited to hear that you're coming here for your studies, so here are a few tips that should make the move easier. The best area to live in is Riverside, because it is safe, lively, and only a short bus ride from the university. If your budget is tighter, you could look at a shared apartment in West End, which has plenty of student housing, supermarkets, and cheap cafés.

What I really like about this city is that it feels busy without being stressful. There is always something going on, from weekend food markets to free outdoor concerts in the summer, yet it is also easy to get around on foot or by bike. Another huge advantage is the mix of old buildings and modern spaces, which gives the place a lot of character.

When you arrive, I would be happy to help in any way I can. I can meet you at the station, help you settle in, and show you around the neighborhood. If you want, I can even ask around about available rooms before you get here.

Best,
Maya

text:
Dear Maya,

Sorry I've been out of touch for so long! A month ago I started a new job as a project coordinator at a small architecture firm, and I've been so busy settling in that I haven't had a moment to write. I wanted you to hear all about it.

My role is to keep our building projects on schedule, which means talking to clients, booking contractors and making sure the designers meet their deadlines. The office is tiny, with only twelve of us, so everyone knows everyone, and my boss has been wonderfully welcoming.

What I love most is the variety, because no two days are ever the same, and I get to visit construction sites, which is fascinating. My colleagues are great fun, too. The downside is the pressure. Deadlines can be stressful, and I sometimes end up answering emails late in the evening, which I really don't enjoy.

My daily routine has changed completely. I now get up at six to catch the train, and I'm rarely home before seven, so I've had to give up my evening yoga class. On the plus side, I've become much better at planning my time!

Write back and tell me your news. Let's meet up soon!

Lots of love,
Elena

My daily routine has changed completely. I now get up at six to catch the train, and I'm rarely home before seven, so I've had to give up my evening yoga class. On the plus side, I've become much better at planning my time!

Write back soon and tell me your news. Let's meet up soon!

Lots of love,
Elena

adjudication.note: Own reading: "soon" twice in a row.

text:
Dear Emma,

I need to tell you something awful about the camera you kindly lent me for my trip to Seattle. On my second day, I took it with me on a ferry ride to Bainbridge Island. As I was getting off the boat, someone bumped into me from behind, and the camera slipped out of my hand onto the metal deck.

It still turns on, but the lens is cracked and the focus is not working properly, so the pictures come out blurry. I felt terrible the moment it happened, especially because you trusted me with it and I know it is one of your favorite things to take when you travel.

I am really sorry, Emma. I should have kept the strap around my wrist the whole time, and I completely understand if you are upset.

I have already taken it to a repair shop, and they said they can replace the lens by next week. Of course, I will pay the full cost. If the repair does not restore it properly, I will buy you the same model or give you the money for a replacement.

Best,
Maya

issues.correction: I need to tell you something awful about the camera
issues.reason: "I am writing because" is stiff and formal for a letter to a close friend.

issues.quote: it has always been one of your favorite things to use when you travel
issues.correction: I know it is one of your favorite things to take when you travel
issues.reason: The original wording is awkward and unidiomatic.

text:
Dear Sophie,

I hope you're doing well! I'm writing because I'm organizing a reunion for our old class, and I'd love you to be part of it. It will take place on Saturday, June 14, at the Garden Room above the Riverside Café, starting at 6 p.m. There'll be a buffet dinner, some music, and a slideshow of photos from our final year.

The trouble is that I can't manage everything alone. My new job has been incredibly busy lately, and I've also been struggling to track down some of our classmates. Half of them seem to have moved to other cities, and I don't have their contact details. On top of that, there's still plenty to arrange before the big night.

You were always the best organizer in our class, so I was wondering whether you could help. Could you contact the people you're still in touch with and ask them to confirm by the end of May? It would also be wonderful if you could dig out any old photos for the slideshow, since I know you kept loads.

Please let me know what you think soon!

Lots of love,
Emma

text:
Dear Emma,

I wanted to tell you all about Josh and Megan’s wedding since I know you were so disappointed to miss it. It was held in a beautiful old country house just outside the city, with the ceremony in a garden full of white roses and fairy lights. Megan looked stunning in a simple satin dress, and Josh was trying hard not to cry when he saw her walking up the aisle.

The whole day felt really relaxed and happy. After the ceremony, we had drinks on the lawn while a jazz trio played, and later everyone moved inside for dinner and dancing. I enjoyed the speeches most of all, especially Josh’s. He managed to be funny and heartfelt at the same time, and by the end half the room was in tears.

There was lots of news about people you know too. Claire has just started a new job in Chicago and seems to love it. Ben and Alicia are expecting a baby in February, which was a lovely surprise, and Daniel has finally gotten engaged.

I hope we can catch up soon so I can show you the photos.

Best,
Lily

issues.quote: Hope we can catch up soon, and I’ll show you the photos.
issues.correction: I hope we can catch up soon, and I’ll show you the photos.
issues.reason: The sentence is clumsy because its two halves do not fit together smoothly; restructuring it, for example as 'I hope we can catch up soon so I can show you the photos', would read better.

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a washing machine I ordered from your website on May 3. The model was a SilverWash 8 kg front-loading machine, order number WS-41827, priced at $649, including installation and removal of my old appliance. According to the confirmation email, delivery was scheduled for May 10.

Unfortunately, the machine did not arrive until May 24, two weeks later. During that period, I received no clear explanation, despite contacting your helpline twice. This delay caused considerable inconvenience, as I had already disposed of my previous machine and had to use a local laundromat for essential washing.

When the appliance was finally installed, I noticed that the left side panel was badly dented and the door did not close properly. In addition, after a short test cycle, water began leaking onto the floor, which suggests that the machine was damaged before or during transit.

I would therefore like you to arrange an immediate replacement and collect the faulty unit at no extra cost. I also expect a full refund of the installation fee, together with reasonable compensation for the delay.

Yours faithfully,
Michael Carter

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to express my concern about the deteriorating condition of Maple Grove Park, which is close to my home. I hope that the department will consider the suggestions I make below.

I have used the park for more than ten years, and I currently visit it four or five times a week. I usually jog there early in the morning, and on weekends I bring my young daughter to the playground and then relax on a bench with a book.

Unfortunately, the park has been neglected recently. The grass has not been cut for weeks, and litter is overflowing from the few bins that remain. Several benches are broken, and one of the swings in the playground has a snapped chain, which poses a real danger to children. In addition, two lamps along the main path no longer work, so the area feels unsafe after dark.

I would therefore suggest that a maintenance team be scheduled to visit the park at least once a week. Installing more bins and repairing the playground equipment and lighting should be treated as priorities. Finally, inviting residents to report problems online might help the department respond more quickly.

I would be grateful for your prompt attention to this matter.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Harper

Dear Ms. Patel,

I am writing to request a week of leave next month to attend my sister’s wedding, which will take place in Seattle. As the oldest sibling, I am responsible for several arrangements before the ceremony, and my family has asked me to be present for the entire week.

If possible, I would like to take leave from Monday, June 10, to Friday, June 14, and return to work on Monday, June 17. I have checked our team calendar, and these dates do not appear to conflict with any major client deadlines.

To ensure that my absence causes as little disruption as possible, I can complete the monthly sales report in advance and send the final version before I leave. I have also spoken with Daniel, who is willing to monitor urgent client emails and handle routine follow-ups during that week.

In addition, I will prepare a clear handover note covering current accounts, pending tasks, and any issues that may require attention. If needed, I will also be available by phone for anything that cannot wait until my return.

Kind regards,
Emily Carter

issues.reason: "Eldest" is the idiomatic word for the oldest of siblings, although "oldest" is acceptable in American English; this is a minor point.

adjudication.note: Proofreader: "oldest sibling" is correct (the reviewer says so itself); kept.

text:
Dear Mr. Harris,

I am writing to you about the recent change to our training schedule. I have been a member of the club for almost six years, and during that time I have always valued the friendly atmosphere and the dedication of our coaches.

Unfortunately, the new schedule has created difficulties for many of us. Sessions now begin at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, which is far too early for anyone who works full time. I rarely finish before 5:30, and several other members have told me they face the same problem. As a result, attendance has dropped noticeably, and some people are even considering leaving the club altogether.

May I suggest a possible solution? If the weekday sessions started at 7:00 p.m., most members would be able to attend after work, and the floodlights on the main field would make evening practice perfectly safe. Alternatively, you could keep one afternoon session for students and retired members and add a second session in the evening. A short survey would show which option people prefer.

Thank you very much for considering my suggestion. I would be glad to help in any way I can.

Yours sincerely,

Daniel Brooks

Dear Emma,

I've finally settled into the new place, and I wanted to tell you all about it. The house is smaller than my old one, but it is bright and cozy, with a tiny back garden that gets the morning sun. My favorite room is the kitchen because it opens onto a little patio, so I can drink coffee outside. The town itself is lovely too. It is much quieter than the city, with tree-lined streets, a huge park by the river, and a fantastic weekend market.

You should definitely come and stay for a few days once you are free. The spare room is ready, and the train journey is only about an hour, so it would be an easy trip. If you came next month, the weather would probably still be warm enough for us to spend plenty of time outdoors.

There is loads we could do together. We could rent bikes and explore the riverside trail, try the cafes around the town square, and cook dinner at home one evening with fresh food from the market. There is also a small art museum you would love.

Hope you can make it!

Love,
Lily

issues.quote: I finally settled into the new place
issues.correction: I have finally settled into the new place
issues.reason: The present perfect is needed for a recent action with a present result; the simple past sounds incomplete here.

text:
Dear Maria,

I'm afraid I have some bad news. Your camera was damaged during my trip to the coast, and I wanted you to hear it from me as soon as possible.

On the second day, I was photographing the sunset from some rocks near the harbor. The ground was wet, and I slipped. The camera swung off my shoulder and hit a boulder. The lens cracked, and now it won't focus properly. Luckily the body still turns on, and I managed to save all the photos on the memory card.

I'm so sorry, Maria. You trusted me with something precious, and I feel awful that I wasn't more careful. I know how much that camera means to you, especially after the portraits you took with it last spring.

Please let me put things right. I've already found a repair shop in town that can replace the lens, and they've quoted me a fair price. I'll pay for everything, of course. If the camera can't be fixed properly, I'll buy you a new one. I'll also copy my best photos for you, because some of them turned out beautifully.

Can I drop by this weekend to talk it over?

With love and apologies,
Daniel
